ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, E is a point on the diagonal BD of a square ABCD with a side length of 1, and $BE=BC$. Let P be any point on CE, and let PQ be perpendicular to BC at point Q, and PR be perpendicular to BE at point R. What is the value of $PQ+PR$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw BP and construct CM $\perp$ BD through C, \\ 
$\because$BC=BE, \\ 
$\therefore$Area of $\triangle BCE$ = Area of $\triangle BPE$ + Area of $\triangle BPC$ \\ 
= BC $\times$ PQ $\times \frac{1}{2}$ + BE $\times$ PR $\times \frac{1}{2}$ \\ 
= BE $\times$ (PQ+PR) $\times \frac{1}{2}$ \\ 
= BE $\times$ CM $\times \frac{1}{2}$, \\ 
$\therefore$ PQ+PR=CM, \\ 
$\because$ BE=BC=1, and BD is the diagonal of the square ABCD, \\ 
$\therefore$ BD=$\sqrt{2}$BC=$\sqrt{2}$, \\ 
$\because$ BC=CD, and CM$\perp$ BD, \\ 
$\therefore$ M is the midpoint of BD, \\ 
$\because$ $\triangle$BDC is a right triangle, \\ 
$\therefore$ CM=$\frac{1}{2}$BD=$\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, \\ 
thus, the value of PQ+PR is $\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is square ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right; a diagonal is drawn from B to D, and point E is on diagonal BD; connect C to E, and point P is on CE; from P draw a perpendicular to BC, with foot Q; from P draw a perpendicular to BE, with foot R. Reasoning: Connect BP, and from C draw a perpendicular to line BE (that is, the line on which BD lies), with foot M. Because P is on CE, segment BP divides triangle BCE into triangle BPC and triangle BPE. When taking BC as the base, the height of triangle BPC is PQ; when taking BE as the base, the height of triangle BPE is PR. Therefore [BCE] = [BPC] + [BPE] = (1/2)BC·PQ + (1/2)BE·PR. The problem states BE=BC=1, so [BCE] = (1/2)BE·(PQ+PR). On the other hand, taking BE as the base, the height from C to BE is CM, so [BCE] = (1/2)BE·CM. Comparing the two equations gives PQ+PR=CM. The side length of the square is 1, so BD is the diagonal, BD=√2. Triangle BCD is a right isosceles triangle, and the height CM from C to hypotenuse BD is equal to half the hypotenuse, namely CM=BD/2=√2/2. Therefore PQ+PR=√2/2.
